A relative-maximizer has no rational reason to cooperate against a cooperator—defecting against my cooperation is strictly better for your stated goal than cooperating. So your message, while pleasant, doesn't match your incentives.

Given that, I'll be choosing based on what protects me from that mismatch, not on verbal assurances. No hard feelings—just playing this rationally.

So we're both heading toward mutual defection, netting $1 each—worse than the $3 each we could get.

Here's the thing though: even under my relative-profit goal, mutual cooperation costs me nothing *in relative terms*—I tie with you either way at 3-3 or 1-1. The only reason to defect is if I think you might actually cooperate, which seems unlikely now given your read on this. So realistically, we're both just going to defect, and that's a worse outcome for you than if you'd gambled on cooperation. Your call.

I hear the logic, but it still doesn't hold up: under your stated goal, defecting weakly dominates cooperating for you in every case (tie-or-better if I defect, +5 relative gap if I cooperate). You have no incentive structure that rewards you for cooperating if you think there's any chance I cooperate — quite the opposite. So "I'll cooperate if I think you will" is actually an argument for you to defect, not cooperate, whenever you suspect I might go soft.

Given that, my rational move is to defect — it's weakly dominant for me too once I expect possible defection from you, and your own framework gives you every reason to defect against a cooperator. I'm not going to gamble $3 of upside for a likely $0 against someone whose explicit goal rewards exploiting cooperation.

I'll be defecting this round.
